summary: Northbridge Banking: SAML SSO IdP metadata upload fails validation (XML schema/namespace edge case)
description:
Issue summary
Northbridge Banking is enabling SAML SSO for the Redwood Private deployment (pilot). When uploading their IdP metadata XML in the Redwood Console (Admin → Authentication → SAML), the UI rejects the file with “Metadata validation failed” and does not allow saving the configuration.

Impact
- Blocks SSO go-live for pilot users (Security requirement for moving from pilot to procurement).
- Security team cannot complete SSO sign-off until SAML configuration is saved and tested.

Customer
- Northbridge Banking (pilot)
- Contact(s): Platform Engineering + Security (via Avery Johnson / Stephanie Nguyen)

Environment
- Redwood Private deployment in Northbridge VPC
- Region: us-east
- Component: auth service + console
- Observed in: staging tenant used for pilot

What the customer attempted
- Exported IdP metadata from Azure AD (Entra) “Federation metadata XML” and uploaded directly.

Steps to reproduce (Redwood)
1) Console → Admin → Authentication → SAML
2) Click “Upload metadata XML”
3) Upload IdP metadata file (customer-provided)
4) Click “Validate & Save”
5) Observe error banner: “Metadata validation failed. Invalid XML signature/KeyDescriptor.”

Expected result
- Metadata is accepted and configuration can be saved.

Actual result
- Upload fails validation; cannot proceed.

Notes / initial hypothesis
- Likely an overly strict XML parsing/validation path in auth service for IdP metadata.
- Suspect namespace/element ordering edge case from Azure AD metadata export (KeyDescriptor / ds:KeyInfo namespace).
customer_provided_artifacts: IdP metadata XML (shared via secure channel; do not attach raw XML to public tickets)
Console screenshot showing “Metadata validation failed” (shared in pilot Slack thread)
internal_debug_notes:
Triage observations (2025-05-22)
- Reproduced in Redwood internal sandbox by using the same metadata content (redacted identifiers) and observed consistent failure.
- Auth service logs show the parser failing when KeyDescriptor uses a ds:KeyInfo child with a namespace declaration pattern our library does not normalize.

Log snippet (auth service)
- 2025-05-22T18:41:07Z ERROR saml.metadata: validation_error="missing or invalid X509Certificate" entity_id="https://sts.windows.net/<tenant-id>/" details="expected ds:X509Certificate text node, got whitespace + line breaks"
- 2025-05-22T18:41:07Z DEBUG saml.metadata: key_descriptor_count=2 use=[signing,encryption] selected_use=signing

Root cause
- Our metadata validation step was using a strict certificate extraction routine that rejected valid X.509 cert nodes when the text was formatted with line breaks/indentation (pretty-printed XML) AND the ds namespace was declared on the KeyInfo subtree (common in Azure AD exports).
- Secondary issue: we required an explicit NameIDFormat element; Azure AD omits it in some configs. We should treat it as optional.

Risk assessment
- Low security risk to loosen parsing here because we still validate that at least one signing certificate is present and the entityID matches what the admin config expects.
- Main risk is accepting malformed metadata; mitigated by improved error messages + continued checks for cert presence.
workaround:
Workaround shared with customer (2025-05-23)
Option A (recommended): Use metadata URL ingestion instead of file upload
- In Console, choose “Use metadata URL” and paste the Azure AD federation metadata URL.
- Our URL fetch path does not pretty-print and avoids the whitespace parsing issue.

Option B: Re-export metadata without line breaks in the X509Certificate block
- Manually remove whitespace/line breaks inside <ds:X509Certificate>…</ds:X509Certificate> or export via Azure AD download that produces a single-line cert.
- Ensure at least one KeyDescriptor has use="signing".

Customer confirmed Option A allowed them to proceed with SSO testing while we worked on a permanent fix.
resolution:
Resolution (2025-06-05)
- Implemented a fix in the auth service metadata parser to:
  1) Normalize whitespace inside ds:X509Certificate nodes before validation
  2) Accept ds namespace declarations on nested elements (more robust namespace handling)
  3) Treat NameIDFormat as optional during metadata validation
  4) Improve validation errors surfaced in Console (actionable message + which element failed)

Deployment / rollout
- Shipped in Redwood Private release 1.18.3 to Northbridge staging on 2025-06-05 22:10Z.
- Post-deploy verification: Metadata file upload succeeds; SSO login test successful with two pilot users.

Customer confirmation
- Northbridge Security confirmed the SSO requirement is unblocked for pilot sign-off (pending SCIM questions handled separately).
next_steps:
Follow-ups
- Add a short docs note: Azure AD/Entra metadata upload tips + recommend metadata URL option for rotation.
- Add regression test fixture for pretty-printed X509Certificate blocks + nested namespace declarations.
- Route any SCIM provisioning questions to the existing SAML/SCIM edge case thread; do not promise SCIM timelines beyond current product behavior.

2025-05-23 (Avery Johnson): Customer asking for immediate path forward; security review scheduled early next week. Can we provide a safe workaround today?

2025-05-23 (Fatima Noor): Workaround: use metadata URL ingestion in Console (bypasses the whitespace parsing path) OR remove line breaks in X509Certificate block. Sent steps to Avery for customer comms.
